scope_note: All seven preserved HTML letters were read in full with headers, bodies, annotations, editorial notes, bibliographies, scholarly sections and figures checked. All are dated 1868 and remain outside 1844-46.

record_reviews.summary: Weir reports a bullfinch attacking a newly introduced bunting and discusses sexual selection in birds and Lepidoptera.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [before 3 March 1868], XML upper bound 1868-03-02; no 1844-46 constraint.

evidence.quote: the only bird which noticed the new arrival was a Bullfinch

record_reviews.summary: Weir clarifies Darwin's sexual-selection question and reports coloration, pugnacity, and female preference observations.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [before 5 March 1868], XML upper bound 1868-03-04; no 1844-46 constraint.

evidence.quote: do the females give a preference for certain males?

record_reviews.summary: Weir reports sex ratios and pugnacity in chaffinches, blackbirds and robins, plus Harrison Weir's starling observations and a branded sheep report.
